claims: It examines the views of Maran in the Shulchan Aruch and the Arizal alongside the historical development of communal practices that sometimes differ from these rulings - 'historical development of communal practices' is background knowledge not derived from the text
summary: This class explores the different customs regarding the congregation's participation in reciting Naqdishakh during the prayer service. It examines the views of Maran in the Shulchan Aruch and the Arizal alongside the historical development of communal practices that sometimes differ from these rulings.
questions: Should the congregation recite Naqdishakh along with the chazzan?
What does the Arizal say about reciting Naqdishakh?
Why do some communities recite the entire Naqdishakh out loud despite other opinions?
What does it mean when a custom supersedes the law?
